source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: CLAVIER picks autoclave loads of composite parts at Lockheed Sunnyvale by retrieving past successful loads. Authors call it one of the first fielded CBR systems.
numbers: Development began March 1989; first version fielded November 1989; v1.0 done September 1990; about 2 person-years; daily use since September 1990; 2-3 loads per day; 2 autoclaves; 6-8 hour cure cycle.
quote: As one of the first fielded case-based reasoning systems, CLAVIER demonstrates CBR to be a practical technology
limits: Self-report by the builders. No controlled comparison with human planners.
agent_relevance: Deployed CBR started small and went live in under a year. Our agent can also start with few seed cases.

source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: Why CBR was chosen: experts could not state rules for mold placement except by recalling a specific past load. A rule-based build and a thermodynamic model were judged infeasible.
numbers: A mold shifted 12-24 inches can leave the target thermodynamic profile. Leader and lagger parts must stay within a 30 F delta (IAAI version) and advance at least 1 degree per minute.
limits: Reasoning of the authors, not a tested comparison.
agent_relevance: Where experts know cases but not rules, store cases. Matches our schema choice to avoid forced rule talk.

source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: Cost of a bad load before CLAVIER, and the claimed payoff. Discrepancy reports from incompatible loads were virtually eliminated.
numbers: Inspection after a discrepancy report: $1000. Scrap: average $2000, some parts $20,000-$50,000. Claimed savings: thousands of dollars each month. No before/after counts given.
limits: No numeric before/after rate; claim is qualitative. Novelty and selection effects not examined.
agent_relevance: Payoff was measured as avoided failures, not as accuracy. A useful framing for an agent that has a hard cost on errors.

source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: Case base starts from the experts' own logbooks and grows by use. Cases are labelled valid or invalid per autoclave, and users edit cases in a graphic editor.
numbers: Seed: expert notebooks (course notes cite about 20 layouts at start and hundreds later; not opened). Validity is context dependent: the same load can be valid in one autoclave and invalid in another.
limits: Case-base size over time is not given in the paper text I read.
agent_relevance: Cases need context labels and a validity flag. Retaining failures as invalid cases is part of the design (negative cases).

source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: Retrieval and validation logic. Retriever ranks loads by three criteria. If no exact match, the user adapts the closest case by hand, then the system validates it against similar valid and invalid cases.
numbers: Criteria: maximise needed parts covered, minimise extra parts, maximise compatibility quality. If likely invalid, it suggests similar valid alternatives or splitting into several loads.
limits: Adaptation is done by the human, not the program. One noted exception: removing molds from a valid load generally stays valid but molds need repositioning.
agent_relevance: Human-in-the-loop revise, with a check against negative cases. Similar to our rule that a pass must rest on something the answer was not fitted to (G3).

source: Hinkle and Toomey (1995) Applying Case-Based Reasoning to Manufacturing (CLAVIER), AI Magazine 16(1)
finding: Lessons learned: users judge the system by usability and tangible benefit, not by the AI technique. Data quality limits the planner.
numbers: Planner scheduling accuracy limited to about one week though designed for several weeks. Most popular feature: printing load reports users used to draw by hand.
limits: Anecdotal.
agent_relevance: Boring plumbing (records, reports) drove adoption. For an agent: output format and logging matter as much as the core method.

source: Hinkle (1994) Clavier, IAAI-94
finding: Conference version of the CLAVIER paper (IAAI-94). Confirms same facts and adds team and training detail.
numbers: Five operators and two support staff use it daily; operators trained by the two expert operators who were on the team; trained users then trained others; extended to Lockheed Georgia facilities.
limits: Same authors and data as the AI Magazine paper; not independent.
agent_relevance: Experts on the development team from day one helped acceptance.

source: Hinkle (1994) Clavier, IAAI-94
finding: Quote on user priorities.
numbers: Hardcopy load reports named as single most popular feature.
quote: users do not care whether the application uses sophisticated artificial intelligence techniques or random guesses
limits: Same as above.
agent_relevance: Adoption lesson.

source: Hennessy and Hinkle (1992) Applying case-based reasoning to autoclave loading, IEEE Expert 7(5):21-26
finding: Original CLAVIER report. Not opened; only bibliographic data seen in search summaries.
numbers: IEEE Expert vol 7 no 5, October 1992, pp 21-26.
limits: Could not read full text this session.
agent_relevance: Primary citation for the first fielded claim.

source: Guo, Liu, Chen et al. (2025) Optimizing CBR System for Functional Test Script Generation with LLMs (Re4), KDD 2025
finding: A deployed LLM+CBR system at Huawei Datacom retrieves 3 past test intent/script pairs, the LLM reuses them, engineers revise, and the pair is retained. Re4 adds reranking-based retriever finetuning and RL finetuning of the reuse step.
numbers: Test scripts are about 40% of functional-test workload; engineers write 1-2 scripts a day. Data: DCN 30,887 and SP 58,429 samples; clean test sets 689 (DCN) and 366 (SP). FF1: DCN CBR 64.67, CBR+SFT 67.87, CBR+Re4 70.11 (+3.30%); SP 55.83, 57.98, 61.92 (+6.80%). Naive SFT lowest (DCN 49.46, SP 38.71).
limits: Single run per method (authors say so). Retriever bge-m3. Offline metric is function F1, not human acceptance.
agent_relevance: Direct modern descendant of CLAVIER-style deployed CBR. Shows case reuse beats finetuning alone when the model must call functions it has not seen.

source: Guo et al. (2025) Re4, KDD 2025: online evaluation and the Retain step
finding: In the live setting, removing Retain (fixed case bank, which equals plain RAG) greatly hurts. Software changes, so new cases are needed.
numbers: About 6,000 recent online samples from the deployed system on 2 units. CBR+Re4 beat the previously deployed CBR+SFT by 2.75% FF1 (DCN) and 10.08% (SP). The w/o-Retain variant fell far below deployed CBR+SFT (figure shows about -78.65% DCN and -69.22% SP average FF1 change).
limits: Acceptance-rate A/B test not run: few users per unit and users differ in taste. Metric is FF1 against revised scripts.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that retention is what separates CBR from RAG in a drifting domain. Supports retaining checked cases.

source: Guo et al. (2025) Re4: human evaluation and repetition
finding: Pairwise human review preferred CBR+Re4 to CBR+SFT on both units. Re4 also cut repetitive generation.
numbers: Repetitive generation reduced by 2.47 points (DCN) and 2.41 (SP); SP rate 0.45%. Removing retriever finetuning cost about 1% FF1. KL coefficient 0.1 best; 0 hurt sharply.
limits: Win/tie/loss rates only shown in a figure. Single runs.
agent_relevance: Retriever tuning gives small gains; reuse alignment gives more.

source: Guo, Deng, Wen, Chen, Chang, Wang (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science with LLMs and Case-Based Reasoning, ICML
finding: DS-Agent runs a CBR loop over Kaggle expert insights in a development stage, then a cheap deployment stage that reuses past successful solutions as one-shot code examples.
numbers: 30 tasks (12 development, 18 deployment). Development: GPT-4 success 100%. Deployment one-pass rate: GPT-3.5 85%, GPT-4 99% vs best baseline 56% and 60%; Mixtral-8x7b 6% to 31%. Cost per run: $0.06 (GPT-3.5) and $1.60 (GPT-4), reduced to $0.0045 and $0.135 in deployment.
limits: Small task set; Kaggle-style tasks; five trials. Authors' own benchmark.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a case bank of past successes lets weak models do well at low cost.

source: DS-Agent (2024) ablations
finding: Removing CBR hurts most; removing revise-by-execution-feedback of the retrieved case hurts less. Whole solved cases beat textual insights.
numbers: Average best rank over 12 development tasks, GPT-4: full 2.08; w/o ReviseRank 2.58; w/o CBR 3.41 (lower is better; five trials). In deployment, learning from past executable solutions beat learning from text insights on nearly all tasks. Zero example cases was the worst setting.
limits: Rank metric, small N of tasks.
agent_relevance: Concrete executable cases beat abstract advice. Execution feedback helps (agrees with G2).

source: Stocker (2026) Towards Persistent Case-Based Memory for Autonomous Data Science (CBR-augmented R&D-Agent, Gemma 4 31B)
finding: Mixed result. CBR memory gave slightly higher and steadier accuracy on one Kaggle task and a worse result on the other.
numbers: Four seeds, eight loops. Spaceship Titanic accuracy 0.8147 vs 0.8098 (d=-1.41 as reported; lower variance, SD 0.0024 vs 0.0042). NOMAD RMSLE (lower better) CBR 0.0632 vs baseline 0.0608 (d=-0.75, p=0.20). Seed KB 60 cases, grew to 67-68. 108 retrieval events: mean embedding similarity 0.882, mean code-fingerprint similarity 0.305.
limits: Preprint, no ablation, tiny N, within-competition cases only. Authors say effect is directional.
agent_relevance: Honest sign that CBR memory can reduce exploration. Variance dropped, ceiling did not rise.

source: Nguyen, Moen, Marttinen (2026) CBR-to-SQL
finding: Splits retrieval into a structure step and an entity-alignment step, then revises. Beats single-step RAG for clinical text-to-SQL, most when data is scarce.
numbers: GPT-4o main, GPT-4.1-mini for ablations. MIMICSQL AccEX 0.899 vs MedTS 0.894 (fine-tuned). With under 10% of training data, EHRSQL gap over RAG-to-SQL was +11.9 AccEX and +10.2 AccLF. CBR-to-SQL at 10% data beat RAG-to-SQL at full data across nearly all metrics. Removing Revision gave a sharp drop.
limits: Preprint under review. Entity-tagging errors propagate.
agent_relevance: Abstract skeleton retrieval plus a revise step generalises better than near-exact match.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: CBR for Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Stores past (error, fix operator) pairs and retrieves by the new error message rather than by the problem text. Beats stateless self-correction.
numbers: HumanEval-Hard Plus pass up to +6.66 points over Momentum (86.67 to 93.33). MBPP-Hard Plus up to +20.51 (58.12 to 78.63). Claims +20.5% MBPP pass and -50.6% tokens on HumanEval vs TextGrad. Cross-domain: problem-based retrieval collapsed to 58.12% Plus on MBPP with HumanEval cases (baseline 48.72); error-based retrieval was +16.24 better.
limits: Small benchmarks; ablation uses MBPP case base for both; authors from industry, no external replication.
agent_relevance: Index cases by the failure signal, not the surface problem. Fits G2 (revise from real output). Surface-similar retrieval overfits.

source: Gan, Dao, Zettsu (2025) CBR-LLM for safety-critical driving decisions
finding: Similarity-based case retrieval beat random case selection for few-shot prompts. A single random example often made models worse than zero-shot.
numbers: Real near-miss dashcam data. 1000 scenarios: 900 in the case base, 100 test (balanced over 7 risk types). Best model Llama 3.3 70B micro-accuracy 0.937 risk-unaware and 0.941 risk-aware without cases. Compared 1, 3, 5 shots.
limits: Exact CBR gain per model is in a figure; not extracted. Labels are human driver actions, not outcomes.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant cases can mislead the model (1-shot random lower than zero-shot). Retrieve by relevance or give none.

source: Sourati, Ilievski, Sandlin, Mermoud (2023) Case-Based Reasoning with Language Models for Classification of Logical Fallacies, IJCAI
finding: CBR retrieval plus adaptation improved fallacy classification and out-of-domain transfer. Case base size barely mattered, and a small case base was best.
numbers: CBR beat vanilla LMs by 2.5-6 F1 points in-domain and up to 8 out-of-domain, across three LMs; beat few-shot Codex. 10% of case database gave the best result; more cases lowered performance. Retrieved case labels matched the true label only 27.7%.
limits: Older encoder LMs, not chat LLMs. Different case representations changed results by model.
agent_relevance: Retrieved cases act indirectly as evidence, not as labels to copy. More stored cases is not always better (links to case-base maintenance).

source: Fungwacharakorn et al. (2025) Argumentative Reasoning with Language Models on Non-factorized Case Bases (AAM-CBR)
finding: Language models extract factors from raw cases and a symbolic argument step decides. It beats a single-prompt baseline only when the new case has many factors.
numbers: Synthetic credit-card dataset, new cases with 6-10 factors; 10 x 5 = 50 case pairs per test set. GPT-4o slightly better than Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite at factor extraction; accuracy rose with n, biggest jump between 9 and 10 factors.
limits: Synthetic data, small, initial experiments.
agent_relevance: Single-prompt LLMs handle few-factor cases but degrade as factors grow; put the combining step in code (G5).

source: Wang et al. (2026) DomAgent: Knowledge Graphs and CBR for Domain-Specific Code Generation
finding: Adds case retrieval plus a knowledge graph. Small open models close the gap on a real truck-software task.
numbers: DS-1000 pass@1: DomAgent Qwen2.5-7B 39.2%, LLaMA3.1-8B 40.5%, GPT-4o 51.0%. Truck CAN signal task: GPT-4o 71.22% alone, 98.04% with DomRetriever; DomAgent Qwen2.5-7B 96.64% vs its vanilla 39.62%.
limits: Industrial dataset small and private; authors' benchmark.
agent_relevance: Case retrieval helps most in narrow domains missing from training data. Matches deployed-CBR pattern.

source: CBR for FinQA numerical reasoning (2024), arXiv 2405.13044
finding: Retrieving similar question-program cases improves a program generator on FinQA. Baseline errors: 48% are wrong operations.
numbers: FinQA 8,281 pairs (6,251 train, 883 val, 1,147 test). Combining question and program as retrieval input helped retrieval. One table row: Exe Acc 56.10 62.51 59.02 54.14 58.15 across variants (variant labels not captured).
limits: Weak paper (thesis style, encoder models). Numbers not mapped to variants.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. Cite only for the 48% operation-error statistic.

source: Review of Case-Based Reasoning for LLM Agents (2025), arXiv 2504.06943
finding: Review proposing CBR inside LLM agents and comparing with chain-of-thought and RAG. Only the abstract was read.
numbers: No numbers extracted.
limits: Theoretical; abstract only.
agent_relevance: Pointer for background. Not evidence.

source: Cross-source synthesis for deployed CBR (c01-c13)
finding: Across 1989 CLAVIER and 2025 Huawei, the same pattern: small seed cases from real work, a human revise step, retention of checked cases, and benefit tied to a domain where rules are hard to write.
numbers: CLAVIER: live within about 8 months of start. Huawei: Retain removal cost far more than retriever finetuning (about 1% FF1).
limits: No deployed CBR source here reports a controlled human-vs-system trial with sample sizes.
agent_relevance: Keep case retention and human revise; do not expect fancy retriever tuning to matter much.

source: Cross-source synthesis for LLM CBR failure modes (c15-c19)
finding: CBR in LLM loops can fail: irrelevant cases mislead, large case bases can lower accuracy, memory can reduce exploration.
numbers: Random 1-shot below zero-shot (driving); 10% case base best (fallacies); NOMAD CBR worse than baseline (0.0632 vs 0.0608).
limits: Three small studies, different models and tasks.
agent_relevance: Gate retrieval by relevance and cap the case bank. Test against a no-memory control.

source: CLAVIER as a negative-case system (synthesis of Hinkle and Toomey 1995)
finding: CLAVIER validates new loads by similarity to both valid and invalid cases, an early use of failure cases that LLM agents rediscovered.
numbers: Invalid cases drive 'likely incompatible' warnings and split suggestions.
limits: Mechanism described, performance not reported separately.
agent_relevance: Store failed attempts with the failing output and retrieve them as warnings.

source: CLAVIER versus 2025 LLM CBR: who does Adapt (synthesis)
finding: CLAVIER left adaptation to the human, then validated. Re4 and DS-Agent let the LLM adapt, with a human or execution feedback checking.
numbers: CLAVIER user edits; Huawei engineers revise; DS-Agent execution feedback ablation 2.08 vs 2.58 rank.
limits: Different domains.
agent_relevance: Model adapts, program or human checks (our Section 1 split).

source: Guo et al. (2025) Re4: why CBR over finetuning or RAG in test generation
finding: Authors argue CBR differs from RAG because it retrieves problem-solution pairs for analogical reuse and keeps updating the bank.
numbers: Naive SFT scored below naive CBR on both units (DCN FF1 49.46 vs 64.01; SP 38.71 vs 54.60) because the model must call functions beyond its knowledge.
limits: Authors' framing.
agent_relevance: Cases supply knowledge training cannot add quickly.
